newsitem.title: UK: Budget fails to boost UK Conservatives - poll.
newsitem.headline: Budget fails to boost UK Conservatives - poll.

text.p: Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke's annual budget failed to boost the election chances of Britain's ruling Conservatives who are still almost 20 percentage points behind the opposition Labour Party, the latest poll showed.
The opinion poll for Tuesday's Guardian newspaper gave Labour 50 percent, up three percentage points on November, and the Conservatives on 31 percent, down five points.
The centrist Liberal Democrats stayed steady at 15 percent. Others were also unchanged on four percent.
Clarke cut income tax by one percent in his budget, the last before an election that has to be called by next May. The Conservatives have now been in power for 17 years.
But the Conservatives gained some comfort from the poll -- most voters believed they were more likely than Labour to be able to keep taxes low.
